extracted.intended_audience: NIH F31 predoctoral fellowship applicants, sponsors/mentors, and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Summary Statement / peer review critique used to evaluate an NIH F31 predoctoral fellowship application, listing criterion scores, reviewer critiques (strengths/weaknesses), and administrative determinations (human/animal protection, biohazards, resource sharing, budget).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: (summary evaluation of the application; reviewers assign an overall impact score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language from critiques: summarizes applicant, sponsor, mentors, environment, and research plan; e.g., 'extraordinary applicant, outstanding sponsor and mentors, exceptional environment and thoughtful research plan provide a tremendous opportunity for an excellent foundation for a future independent research career.' Impact Score is calculated after discussion by averaging overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship Applicant: evaluation of the applicant's qualifications, prior training/productivity, academic performance, commitment to career path, and letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list strengths and weaknesses (bulleted). Examples drawn from critiques: Strengths include commitment to career with MS from Johns Hopkins, multiple abstract presentations, co-authorships, excellent grades, strong letters endorsing hard work and productivity, outstanding productivity (multiple coauthorships and manuscripts), independence, critical thinking, and honors/activities. Weaknesses: generally 'None noted' in these critiques. Score examples: criterion scores of '1' indicate outstanding applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants: evaluation of the mentoring team, sponsor's expertise, funding record, productivity, and training record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note strengths/weaknesses: Strengths include outstanding mentoring team with complementary expertise, sponsor well-funded (KO8, Burroughs Wellcome, pending R01), productive with high-impact publications, co-mentor with strong training record, strong dissertation committee and collaborators. Weaknesses noted: primary mentor has no previous sponsored trainees or limited training record (but mitigated by inclusion of senior mentors). Criterion scores in examples: '2' or '1' depending on reviewer. Include explicit mention of mentor's prior training record as an evaluative factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Training Plan: evaluation of the scientific and training merits of the proposed research, hypothesis, preliminary data, experimental design, pitfalls/alternatives, aims, and training opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cite strengths such as strong preliminary data, hypothesis-driven proposal, well-designed experiments with pitfalls and alternatives, complementary aims, clinically relevant problem, innovative models (e.g., mouse osteomyelitis model), and an impressive range of techniques. Weaknesses in examples: minor concerns such as lack of applicant mastery of specialized surgical technique (sponsor will carry out surgery), sensitivity issues in assays with low cell numbers, and that a brief summary of the mouse model in the proposal would be helpful. Criterion scores shown as '2' in critiques for Research Training Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Potential: assessment of how the proposed fellowship will advance the applicant's development toward an independent research career, including new skills, career development activities, and mentoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: project expands applicant's expertise (e.g., from viral to bacterial models and genetic mouse models), detailed training plan (meetings, seminar series, career development, mentoring), institutional programs (Vanderbilt Program in Molecular Medicine, ASPIRE Module), funded opportunities for cross-training, and letters attesting to mentoring commitment. Weaknesses: typically 'None noted' in these critiques. Criterion scores examples: '1' or '2' depending on reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Environment & Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional Environment & Commitment to Training: evaluation of the host institution's resources, programs, and demonstrated commitment to supporting the trainee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers highlight strengths such as outstanding biomedical environment, groups of relevant researchers, institutional funding for pilot work and mini-sabbaticals, BRET office resources (IDP program, RCR training, career activities), and participation in programs that enhance clinical exposure for basic researchers. Weaknesses: none noted in these critiques. Criterion scores examples: '1'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections for Human Subjects: determination of applicability and adequacy of protections when human subjects are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this application: 'Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)'. Guidance: if human subjects are involved, reviewers evaluate protections; here status is recorded as NA and Human Subjects line shows '10-No human subjects involved' (administrative code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals: evaluation of the use of vertebrate animals and whether the animal protocol addresses required points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented as 'YES, all four points addressed' and reviewers/SRO note 'Well justified and described in detail' and 'A very detailed, complete discussion is included that covers all four points.' Also summary: 'Vertebrate Animal: ACCEPTABLE' in committee summary. Scoring/concern: reviewers check completeness of justification, procedures, and welfare considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Biohazards: assessment of biosafety concerns, containment, and appropriateness of facilities/training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Acceptable' in critiques. Specific guidance in critiques: 'Facilities and training for BSL-2 work are noted' and 'A good description of the training and facilities for working with a human pathogen is provided.' Reviewers evaluate whether biohazard handling and training are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research: evaluation of the adequacy and appropriateness of proposed RCR training for the trainee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated statuses vary across critiques: marked 'Acceptable' in some critiques, and 'Unacceptable' in one critique that provided details: format described as '2 hour course during orientation plus 9 hour annual symposium', subject matter 'Standard list of topics', faculty participation 'Face to face faculty teaching', duration 'Acceptable; see Format', frequency: one critique noted 'No mention is made of the need for refresher training after 4 years.' Other critiques state ongoing RCR training with lab meeting presentations every 1-2 months covering each RCR area. Scientific Review Officer notes 'Training in the responsible conduct of research was adequately described.' Reviewers evaluate format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Format (Required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on Format (Required): reviewer statement about the format of the training/RCR or other required elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'acceptable' (general short-form comment) and more detailed: '2 hour course during orientation plus 9 hour annual symposium' or 'Faculty lectures and small group discussions of case studies.' Reviewers are required to comment on format and may mark acceptable/unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Subject Matter (Required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on Subject Matter (Required): reviewer statement about the adequacy of content/topics covered in required training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'acceptable' (short form) and 'Covers all relevant areas' (detailed). Reviewers assess whether the subject matter covers required RCR topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Faculty Participation (Required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on Faculty Participation (Required): reviewer statement about faculty involvement in training activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'acceptable', 'Face to face faculty teaching', 'All sessions are conducted by faculty.' Reviewers assess whether faculty actively participate in training and mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Duration (Required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on Duration (Required): reviewer statement about the time allocated to training/RCR activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'acceptable', 'Full-day symposium comprising nine hours', and 'Acceptable; see Format'. Reviewers evaluate whether training time is sufficient and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Frequency (Required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on Frequency (Required): reviewer statement about how often training is provided or refreshed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'acceptable' (short) and more specific: 'In addition to the 11 hours of formal training, she receives ongoing training in RCR with lab meeting presentations covering each of the 9 areas of RCR every 1-2 months.' One critique noted 'No mention is made of the need for refresher training after 4 years.' Reviewers assess adequacy of frequency and refreshers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource Sharing Plans: assessment of plans for sharing data, reagents, and other resources resulting from the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'Acceptable' in this summary. Example guidance: 'Acceptable plans are in place for sharing data and mouse strains.' Reviewers evaluate whether sharing plans are adequate and compliant with NIH policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and Period of Support: reviewer recommendation regarding requested budget and duration of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this summary: 'Recommend as Requested' and 'The budget was recommended as requested.' Reviewers/committee may recommend approval 'as requested' or with modifications; this feeds into funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG Scoring Notes / Impact Score Calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring and calculation notes about peer review process and use of criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH process note from footnote: 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. For details see http://grants.nih.gov/grants/peer_review_process.htm#scoring.' This explains that criterion scores (e.g., 'Fellowship Applicant: 1', 'Research Training Plan: 2') are recorded but the overall impact score is the aggregated numerical measure.
